frontier.hypothesis: The inline-helper chassis's remaining 13 closes if the helper's pointer pseudo survives to cse as a shared two-use base instead of being const-substituted into each mem at inline time. This is the only live axis that reaches the target's access signature from a construct nobody has objected to.
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2's integrate.c copies the inline body with copy_rtx_and_substitute and a const-equivalence map; a local initialised from a SYMBOL_REF is a constant equivalence, so it is propagated into every use inside the copy. Each mem then reaches combine with a single-use address and combine folds %lo into it, producing `lui; lbu 0(reg)` per access instead of the target's one shared unfolded `lui`/`addiu` base. The textual four-handle form does not hit this because its pointer locals are never inlined and survive to cse as shared pseudos.
frontier.next_probe: Confirm the pass first, then attack it. (a) Run cc1 -da on the m1 form (harness already wired at s11/dump.sh and s6's dump scripts) and check whether the address is already substituted in the .rtl dump (integrate) or only after .cse/.combine. (b) If integrate: give the helper's handle a shape the const map cannot equate - e.g. a second natural mem use through `q[0]`, or a nested second inline accessor so the address crosses two inline boundaries, or helper parameter shapes beyond m7's `u8 *` (a `u8 **`). Note m2 (mask factored into a second helper, zero handle declarations in the function body) is 26, so the mask handle must stay in the caller.
